options: Data that has never been analysed because of technology barriers
Data that is used only during audits
Data that is corrupted during transfer
Data that is no more required and of no use anymore
Data duplicated across several systems
questions.explanation: Data Detritus means data which is no longer required and is of no use anymore.

questions.stem: Which description distinguishes Detritus data from Dark data and Dormant data?
options: Detritus data was and is not in use
Detritus data was once in use but will not be in use anymore
Detritus data is hardly in use
Detritus data is used every day
Detritus data is data whose format cannot be read
questions.explanation: Dark data was and is not in use, Dormant data is hardly in use, and Detritus data was in use but will not be anymore.

questions.stem: Why is Detritus data normally not deleted or purged?
options: Because it is too large to delete efficiently
Because it is still used for daily analytics
Because deleting it would break data pipelines
Because it is needed to train new models
Because Regulatory or Compliance parties can still require it
questions.explanation: Although no longer useful for analytics, Detritus data may be demanded by regulators or compliance bodies, so it is retained.

questions.stem: Which banking example illustrates Data Detritus?
options: The first transaction of a customer who has been active with the bank for 20 years
The daily balance of every current account
Card transactions from the last quarter used for fraud detection
The interest rate table for mortgages
Yesterday's ATM withdrawals
questions.explanation: The bank has no analytical need for a long-standing customer's first transaction, yet it cannot purge it because a regulator may ask when and where the customer came on board.

options: Yes, all Dark Data should be purged
Yes, because it never has value
No
Only if it is structured
Only if it is older than five years
questions.explanation: The answer given is a clear No: not all Dark Data is bad, and some can still be required or become useful.

questions.stem: Can all Dark Data be deleted or purged?
options: Always yes
Never
Only structured Dark Data
Yes and No, depending on whether it may still be required
Only after it becomes Dormant
questions.explanation: The answer is Yes and No: some Dark Data can be purged, but some must be kept, for example for regulatory reasons.

questions.stem: Which business model is said to delete or purge most of its data after extracting valuable insights from it?
options: Banking
E-commerce
Government
Healthcare
Insurance
questions.explanation: E-commerce is named as the business model that purges most of its data once the valuable insights have been extracted.

questions.stem: In a nutshell, what should happen to data that was in use in the past compared with the rest?
options: Everything should be kept in the data warehouse forever
Everything should be deleted after one year
Past data should be moved to the operational database
Past data should be re-analysed each quarter
Data that was in use is most probably kept in cold storage, and the rest can be deleted or purged
questions.explanation: Data elements that were used for decision-making are kept in cold storage, while the rest can be deleted or purged.

questions.stem: Compared with Detritus data, what characterises traditional Dark Data?
options: It was never in use because of technology barriers
It was valuable once and then became Dormant
It is always deleted after an audit
It is only found in e-commerce
It is used heavily by regulators
questions.explanation: Detritus data was once valuable before becoming Dormant, whereas traditional Dark Data was never in use due to technology barriers.

questions.stem: Given that Twitter alone processes about 52 terabytes of data daily, what is recommended for such huge social media data rather than keeping all of it forever?
options: Keep all of it in the data warehouse
Purge all of it immediately after collection
Convert the elements that were used for decision-making into Dark data and delete or purge the rest
Move all of it to tape drives permanently
Hand all of it to regulators
questions.explanation: Not all such data needs to be kept forever: the elements used for decision-making can be retained as Dark data while the rest is deleted or purged.
